# Irboard HTTP contract fixtures

`contract.json` is generated by the real Laravel HTTP routes in
`Irboard/tests/Feature/NodeApiContractTest.php`, using the tables from
`database/install.sql` in **in-memory SQLite**. Every credential and hostname
is fictional. Response bodies are base64 to preserve MessagePack bytes.

The source panel is PoriyaVali/Irboard's `feat/mihomo-server-contract` at `5bd1a6e`,
with node host metadata separate from SNI and the HTTP contract test. Fixtures
cover the existing protocol configurations, the `v2ray` alias, and the six
managed Mihomo protocols (HTTP, SOCKS5, Mieru, ShadowQUIC, Sudoku, Snell), plus eligible and
empty user lists in both formats, ETags, an empty alive
object and report acknowledgements. V2bX consumes these in ordinary Go tests;
Irboard independently tests actual device clearing and traffic retry deduplication,
including each managed protocol's user, ban/unban, online-device, traffic and
node-status routes.

To regenerate with both sibling repositories checked out:

```sh
cd ../Irboard
IRBOARD_NODE_CONTRACT_DIR=../V2bX/api/panel/testdata/irboard \
  php vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Feature/NodeApiContractTest.php
cd ../V2bX
GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 go test -race ./api/panel -run TestIrboardGeneratedContract
```

Run PHPUnit through its checked-in configuration; it pins SQLite `:memory:`
and cannot use the panel's production database. Review the regenerated diff
when changing either side of the API. These tests verify the control-plane
contract; they do not assert every client transport or network condition.

## served.json

`served.json` is what Irboard serves for every node its admin forms make:
VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks, Hysteria, Hysteria2, TUIC and AnyTLS, with
each transport and security the forms offer. It is generated by
`Irboard/tests/Feature/ServedNodeContractTest.php`, which saves each node
through the form's admin route, posted as the browser's form encoder sends it.
For each node it holds the config and user list UniProxy gives V2bX (fetched
as V2bX asks for them) and what a subscriber gets: the Clash Meta proxy, the
sing-box outbound and the share link.

`cmd/irboard_served_test.go` starts each node through V2bX's own node
controller on every core `validateSetupCore` accepts for it. Each core is fed
that config and user list, and each client connects through it to an echo
server: mihomo with the Clash Meta proxy, sing-box with the outbound, and Xray
with the share link. It also checks that the wizard's automatic core can
serve the node, and that a client is given no profile only where it cannot
reach the node at all.

To regenerate:

```sh
cd ../Irboard
IRBOARD_NODE_CONTRACT_DIR=../V2bX/api/panel/testdata/irboard \
  php vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Feature/ServedNodeContractTest.php
cd ../V2bX
GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 go test -tags "sing xray hysteria2 with_quic with_grpc with_utls with_wireguard with_acme with_gvisor mdns trusttunnel mihomo" \
  ./cmd -run TestIrboardServedNodesOnEveryCore
```

Without the release tags, sing-box has no QUIC (Hysteria, TUIC) and no uTLS
(REALITY, fingerprints), and what needs them is skipped.
